**Note:** No \(x\) satisfies the equation: it needs \(\sin^{-1}x = \frac{8 + 3\pi}{10} \approx 1.74\), more than \(\frac{\pi}{2}\). The answer shown follows the paper's answer key, the value the algebra gives.

Let \(s = \sin^{-1}x\), so \(\cos^{-1}x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - s\). \(2s - \dfrac{3\pi}{2} + 3s = 4\) gives \(s = \dfrac{8 + 3\pi}{10}\). Then \(2s + 3\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - s\right) = \dfrac{3\pi}{2} - s = \dfrac{12\pi - 8}{10} = \dfrac{6\pi - 4}{5}\).
